question: What possibilities are there under EU law to deviate from specified measures when preventive measures are applied which go beyond the measures specified in EU law?
Under what circumstances can justified doubts be raised about the reliability of the result of a sample (sampling, detection in the laboratory)?
Despite their effectiveness, why are vaccinations completely disregarded in attempts to reduce salmonella in laying hen flocks?
answer: Requirements for the control of Salmonella in flocks of laying hens are laid down in Regulation (EC) No 2160/2003 (1), further implemented by Commission Regulation (EC) No 1177/2006 (2) and Commission Regulation (EU) No 517/2011 (3). EU harmonised requirements for vaccines and the use of antimicrobials in the framework of national control programmes are laid down in Commission Regulation (EC) No 1177/2006.

The inclusion of preventive measures for the control of Salmonella are important elements in the approval of national control programmes in accordance with Article 6 of Regulation (EC) No 2160/2003. The Commission supports preventive measures in general as demonstrated by the endorsement of a Community guide for good practices in pullet rearing and egg laying flocks (4).

National measures that go beyond the EU requirements cannot deviate from other EU requirements (such as sampling or trade restrictions within the framework of Salmonella controls). In order to exclude false-positive initial testing results, the competent authority may lift the restrictions laid down in point D.2 of Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 2160/2003 if the conditions set out in point D.
4 of that Annex are fulfilled. The suspicion of false-positive results is considered exceptional. In case of suspicion of false-negative results, the flock must be resampled immediately.

Vaccination is very effective in the control of Salmonella, and vaccination programmes against Salmonella enteritidis are therefore mandatory in certain situations in accordance with Article 3 of Commission Regulation (EC) No 1177/2006. Even when not mandatory, vaccination of laying hens is widely applied, and its costs are eligible for co-financing by the Commission (5).

Regulation (EC) No 2160/2003 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 November 2003 on the control of salmonella and other specified food-borne zoonotic agents (OJ L 325, 12.12.2003, p. 1).

Commission Regulation (EC) No 1177/2006 of 1 August 2006 implementing Regulation (EC) No 2160/2003 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards requirements for the use of specific control methods in the framework of the national programmes for the control of salmonella in poultry (OJ L 212, 2.8.2006, p. 3).

Commission Regulation (EU) No 517/2011 of 25 May 2011 implementing Regulation (EC) No 2160/2003 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards a Union target for the reduction of the prevalence of certain Salmonella serotypes in laying hens of Gallus gallus and amending Regulation (EC) No 2160/2003 and Commission Regulation (EU) No 200/2010 (OJ L 138, 26.5.2011, p. 45). https://food.ec.europa.
